To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
insufficient sleep duration and poor quality of sleep are significantly associated with a decreased likelihood of psychological positive health in children and adolescents.

sleep time ≥10 h is significantly associated with an increase in the likelihood of reporting no complaints in children and sleep time ≥9 hours is significantly associated with a higher likelihood of overall psychological health and no complaints indicators in adolescents.
sleep quality and sleep duration are important factors that influence the health status of children and adolescents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the association of sleep patterns with indicators of psychological positive health in children and adolescents.
the relationship of sleep with psychological positive health, and health complaints in a representative sample of children and adolescents from a Mediterranean area.
the importance of sleep duration and sleep quality on psychological health in children and adolescents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sleep is a critical factor for the health of children and adolescents.
sleep is a crucial factor in determining the quality of life in the paediatric population.
sleep duration and sleep quality are associated with psychological positive health indicators and health complaints in healthy children and adolescents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more sleep children and adolescents get, the less health problems they have, and the better they feel.
sleep duration and perceived quality of sleep were associated with psychological positive health, and that sleep duration was associated with health complaints.
children and adolescents with better sleep patterns are more likely to report better psychological positive health and less likely to have health complaints.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sleep quality and duration are important predictors of health complaints and psychological positive health, and that sleep should not be ignored as a potential risk factor in children.
sleep quality is an important factor in children and adolescents psychological health, which should be considered in the development of public health policies.
sleep duration and quality should be considered when assessing psychological positive health and having health complaints.
